record.title: Bill No. 2338/2023 on the development, promotion and ethical and responsible use of artificial intelligence based on the centrality of the human person
record.original_title: Projeto de Lei nº 2338, de 2023 – Dispõe sobre o desenvolvimento, o fomento e o uso ético e responsável da inteligência artificial com base na centralidade da pessoa humana
record.summary: Sets national rules for responsible governance of AI systems. It bans 'excessive risk' systems, such as those that exploit vulnerabilities to cause harm, assess personality traits to predict crime, public-authority universal scoring, autonomous weapons and, with exceptions, real-time remote biometric identification in public spaces. High-risk uses bring rights to explanation, contestation and human review, governance measures and algorithmic impact assessments. General-purpose and generative AI developers must assess risk and, for systemic risk, document tests. Synthetic content needs identifiers and serious incidents must be reported, under a national system (SIA) coordinated by the ANPD.

record.notes: Presented in the Federal Senate by Sen. Rodrigo Pacheco on 3 May 2023, with the original ementa 'Dispõe sobre o uso da Inteligência Artificial'; the Senate calls it the 'Marco Legal da Inteligência Artificial'. The Senate's Temporary Internal Committee on Artificial Intelligence (CTIA) approved rapporteur Sen. Eduardo Gomes's substitute (Amendment No. 199) on 5 Dec 2024. On 10 Dec 2024 the Senate plenary approved the substitute, which was definitively adopted in the supplementary round without amendments, and the other Senate AI bills joined to it (PL 5051/2019, 5691/2019, 21/2020, 872/2021, 3592/2023, 210/2024 and 266/2024) were declared prejudicados. The text sent to the Chamber is the Senate's autógrafo of the substitute, signed by Senate President Rodrigo Pacheco on 31 Jan 2025; Ofício SF No. 235 of 17 Mar 2025 sent it to the Chamber of Deputies for review under art. 65 of the Federal Constitution. As adopted by the Senate, the law would enter into force 730 days after publication; the bans of art. 13, the rules for general-purpose and generative AI (Chapter IV, Section V) and the copyright rules (Chapter X, Section IV) 180 days after publication, except art. 62, which would apply at once; and Chapter IX on supervision (except the sanctions of art. 50) and Sections III and V of Chapter X on publication. Civil liability for damage caused by AI stays under the Consumer Defence Code and the Civil Code, with the burden of proof reversed when the victim is hyposufficient or proof is excessively burdensome (arts. 35 to 37), and fines are capped at R$50 million per infraction or, for private legal entities, 2% of gross revenue in Brazil (art. 50). In the Chamber the bill is subject to a plenary vote under the priority regime (art. 151, II, of the Chamber's Rules). On 4 Apr 2025 it was distributed to six committees and, because more than four had jurisdiction on the merits, a Special Committee was created; the committee was constituted on 29 Apr 2025 and Dep. Aguinaldo Ribeiro (PP-PB) was designated rapporteur on 20 May 2025. The committee approved requests for public hearings and seminars in 2025, and further bills were attached to the bill in 2025 and 2026, most recently PL 3060/2026 on 1 Sep 2026. Its Chamber status is 'Aguardando Parecer do(a) Relator(a) na Comissão Especial' (awaiting the rapporteur's report in the Special Committee); no report or substitute has been presented in the Chamber, and the last recorded action is of 2 Sep 2026. The English machine translation given as english_version renders the Senate's revised text ('Minuta') of 19 Dec 2024, the undated draft of the autógrafo with the same reference (ivb/pl23-2338rev), not the signed autógrafo of 31 Jan 2025.

verification.note: Stored copies: the bill text as received by the Chamber of Deputies (camara.leg.br, 'inteiro teor', codteor=2868197, stored 16 Oct 2026; 36 pages, the Senate autógrafo signed 31 Jan 2025 and stamped 'Apresentação: 17/03/2025'), the Chamber bill page (stored 11 Oct 2026; the archiver found its text unchanged on 16 Oct 2026), the Federal Senate bill page (senado.leg.br, stored 16 Oct 2026; it differs from the 11 Oct copy only in its news sidebar) and an English machine translation published by Campos Thomaz Advogados. Summary, topics, title and original_title were written from the Portuguese text. The Chamber page confirms the number, the ementa, the author, the receipt on 17 Mar 2025, the Special Committee and rapporteur, the status 'Aguardando Parecer do(a) Relator(a) na Comissão Especial', no reports or substitutes in the Chamber and the last action of 2 Sep 2026. The Senate page confirms presentation on 3 May 2023, the CTIA approval of Amendment No. 199 on 5 Dec 2024, final adoption on 10 Dec 2024 and the remittance with Ofício SF 235/2025; it was stored as the record's secondary source, so the presentation date rests on alt-official evidence. The translation is marked 'Machine Translated by Google', is not reviewed and contains errors (its art. 13 renders 'sistemas de IA' as 'information systems'); it was not used for the summary. No English text of the issuer and no government translation was found. The secondary_url now points to the stored bill text; the Senate page, the only stored source of the 3 May 2023 date, leaves the record's local copy and should be requested again in extra_urls by a later refresh. Press reports on the timing of a Chamber vote rest on no stored source and are no longer stated in the record.

summary.quote: Art. 1º Esta Lei estabelece normas gerais de caráter nacional para a governança responsável de sistemas de inteligência artificial (IA) no Brasil
Seção II Do Risco Excessivo Art. 13. São vedados o desenvolvimento, a implementação e o uso de sistemas de IA:

c) avaliar os traços de personalidade, as características ou o comportamento passado, criminal ou não, de pessoas singulares ou grupos, para avaliação de risco de cometimento de crimes
pelo poder público, para avaliar, classificar ou ranquear as pessoas naturais, com base no seu comportamento social ou em atributos da sua personalidade, por meio de pontuação universal
III – em sistemas de armas autônomas (SAA); IV – em sistemas de identificação biométrica à distância, em tempo real e em espaços acessíveis ao público, com exceção das seguintes hipóteses:
Art. 14. Considera-se de alto risco o sistema de IA empregado para as seguintes finalidades e contextos de usos

I – direito à explicação sobre a decisão, a recomendação ou a previsão feitas pelo sistema; II – direito de contestar e de solicitar a revisão de decisões, recomendações ou previsões de sistema de IA; III – direito à revisão humana das decisões
o desenvolvedor e o aplicador, ao introduzirem ou colocarem em circulação no mercado sistema de alto risco, adotarão, entre outras, as seguintes medidas de governança

Art. 25. A avaliação de impacto algorítmico de sistemas de IA é obrigação do desenvolvedor ou do aplicador que introduzir ou colocar sistema de IA em circulação no mercado, sempre que o sistema ou o seu uso forem de alto risco

Art. 29. O desenvolvedor de sistemas de IA de propósito geral e generativa deverá realizar, além da documentação pertinente sobre o desenvolvimento do sistema, sua avaliação preliminar, a fim de identificar seus respectivos níveis de risco esperados, inclusive potencial risco sistêmico.
II – documentar os testes e as análises realizados, a fim de identificar e gerenciar riscos razoavelmente previsíveis
Art. 19. Quando o sistema de IA gerar conteúdo sintético, deverá, considerando o estado da arte do desenvolvimento tecnológico e o contexto de uso, incluir identificador em tais conteúdos
Art. 42. O agente de IA comunicará, em prazo a ser estabelecido, à autoridade setorial a ocorrência de grave incidente de segurança
I – a Autoridade Nacional de Proteção de Dados (ANPD), autoridade competente que coordenará o SIA;

judgment.status_reasoning: Latest event: the Chamber of Deputies page gives the situation 'Aguardando Parecer do(a) Relator(a) na Comissão Especial' and, as the last legislative actions, the attachment of PL 3060/2026 on 1 Sep 2026 and an attachment between two other attached bills (PL 1542/2026 to PL 904/2026) on 2 Sep 2026. The page lists no reports, substitutes or votes in the Chamber ('Histórico de Pareceres, Substitutivos e Votos ( 0 )'), and the archiver found its text unchanged on 16 Oct 2026. The Senate finished its part on 10 Dec 2024 and its page shows the last state '17/03/2025 - REMETIDA À CÂMARA DOS DEPUTADOS'. The stored text is the bill as received for review, with an entry-into-force clause counted from a publication that has not happened. The bill is therefore still pending in the reviewing house: status Draft / proposed, legal_force Proposed, date_in_force null.
judgment.scope_reasoning: In scope without a scope note: Brazil's general AI bill, a pending bill on AI risk governance (AGENTS.md section 10 includes pending bills).
judgment.local_copy_reasoning: Three stored official pages compete for two slots. The Chamber bill page (official_url, unchanged) is the page a later refresh needs: the bill now moves only in the Chamber, so the status, a Chamber substitute (date_last_updated) and any sanction (date_in_force) will appear there first, and as the record's official source it gives official evidence for title, identifier and status. The bill's own text should be the other slot, so secondary_url becomes the stored Chamber 'inteiro teor' (codteor=2868197), the autógrafo the Chamber is reviewing; it supports the title, original_title, summary and topics, and as a secondary source counts as alt-official. The cost is date_published: 3 May 2023 appears only on the Senate page (neither the Chamber page nor the bill text shows it), which leaves the local copy. In this run the level is B either way, because the Senate page was stored as the record's secondary source. A later refresh should list https://www25.senado.leg.br/web/atividade/materias/-/materia/157233 in extra_urls to support date_published; stored then as an extra from an official host it would count as official, and with title and status from the Chamber page the level could be A. The alternative, the Senate page as official_url and the bill text as secondary_url, would give date_published official evidence but drop the Chamber page, which no longer tracks any change on the Senate side, so a later refresh would miss the Chamber's report, committee vote and plenary vote.

changes.title: Rendered from the full ementa of the stored text; the earlier title left out 'based on the centrality of the human person' (com base na centralidade da pessoa humana).
changes.original_title: The number in the form both chambers use in full ('Projeto de Lei nº 2338, de 2023', as on the Chamber page) followed by the ementa verbatim from the stored text; 'nº 2338/2023' does not appear in that form on any stored page.
changes.summary: Rewritten from the stored Portuguese text (arts. 1, 6, 13, 14, 18, 19, 25, 29, 30, 42 and 45), using the bill's own terms: 'excessive risk' (risco excessivo), 'high risk' (alto risco), general-purpose and generative AI (IA de propósito geral e generativa), systemic risk (risco sistêmico), synthetic content (conteúdo sintético), serious incidents (grave incidente), the SIA and the ANPD as competent authority. Moved liability and fines to the notes.
changes.safety_topics: Six topics, each backed by a provision: risk-based classification (arts. 12-15), prohibited practices (art. 13), general-purpose / frontier AI (arts. 29-30), human oversight (arts. 6 and 8), transparency & labelling (art. 19), incident reporting (art. 42). Dropped 'accountability & liability': the record had seven topics, one more than allowed, and the liability chapter mostly keeps the existing Consumer Defence Code and Civil Code regimes (arts. 35-36); the liability and fine provisions are now in the notes.
changes.english_version: The only English text found: a Google machine translation of the Senate's revised text of 19 Dec 2024, published by Campos Thomaz Advogados (third-party); stored in this run.
changes.secondary_url: Points the record's second source at the stored bill text, so that the local copy holds the bill's own text; see local_copy_reasoning.
changes.date_last_updated: The last new version of the text is the Senate substitute definitively adopted on 10 Dec 2024; the 2 Sep 2026 entry was an attachment of other bills, not a new version of PL 2338/2023.
changes.notes: Rewritten from the stored pages and text: adds the CTIA approval, the Senate's final adoption and the bills declared prejudicados, the autógrafo of 31 Jan 2025, the Ofício and art. 65 review, the phased entry into force of art. 80, the liability and fine provisions, the Chamber's distribution, Special Committee and priority regime, the 2026 attachments, the absence of a Chamber report and the version the English translation renders. Removed the press reports on the timing of a vote and the remark that Chamber amendments send the bill back to the Senate, which no stored source shows, and the sentence on the excluded PBIA, which was about the research, not the bill.
changes.verification.note: Describes the four stored files, what each confirms, the quality of the translation and the change of secondary_url.
